text:
carla: Heads-up: I'm planning an RBAC tightening for private deploys tomorrow - removing the wildcard keystore:decrypt permission from the default node-role. Need quick sanity-checks on KMS access patterns, network policies, and audit coverage before we flip it.
ben: +1 on reducing blast radius. main concerns: agents that did implicit decrypts (metrics exporters, sidecars). Do we have inventory of who calls keystore decrypt in prod-priv-vpc?
alice: Inventory is partial. Ran a quick k8s audit last week but it didn't include on-prem satellite clusters. We should require explicit svcacct annotations and update our admission webhook to reject ambiguous perms.
dave: Ops note - if we tighten without netpol updates, key-agent calls to our KMS proxy (10.7.3.12:8443) will fail. Suggest a staged rollout: 1) enable RBAC deny in canary namespace, 2) monitor decrypt errors 3) apply netpol allow rules for authorized pods only.
carla: Agreed on staged. Ben can you share a short-netpol snippet we can apply during canary? Want minimal egress so it's easy to revert.
ben: Here is minimal egress rule we use in hosted -> private mapping (will paste to infra repo):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-kms-proxy-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: key-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.7.3.12/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443
```
carla: Nice, keep it tight. Also need to confirm audit logs capture the decrypt caller identity and request id so we can trace failures to a pod. Alice?
alice: Our audit pipeline captures KMS API calls in control plane logs but we need to ensure keystore shim also forwards the original pod/serviceaccount in the KMS request metadata. Filing a small change: keystore-shim add X-Caller-SA header when contacting proxy.
dave: Ops-bot will throw alerts if decrypt failures spike. We should add a temporary alert rule:
- metric: kms.decrypt.fail_count
- scope: prod-priv-* canary namespaces
- threshold: >5 in 5m -> page oncall
ops-bot: ALERT triggered: 3 decrypt failures in prod-priv-canary at 1729509990. Details: namespace=prod-priv-canary, pod=ml-runner-3, svcacct=ml-runner-sa.
carla: Thanks for the auto alert - exactly why we stage. Can someone check if those failures are expected? Could be missing svcacct annotation or netpol.
ben: Looking at logs - requests reached KMS proxy but were 403 from keystore layer: "caller not authorized". That indicates RBAC prevented decrypt before reaching external KMS. So likely the node-role removal hit the shim.
alice: If orders are 403 at shim, add fallback: allow a temporary per-node decrypt bind for the canary nodes for 1 hour while we fix svcacct->role mapping. I'll open a short-lived grant CR.
dave: I'll apply netpol and the temp grant in canary now, monitor for recoveries. If we see success we proceed to step 2.
carla: Also tagging this for vuln triage - one of the reasons for tightening was the recent KMS-agent CVE-2024-4123 exploit vector. We need to ensure our mitigation (least-priv roles + audit) satisfies compliance. Alice, can you write the two-line justification for SOC report?
alice: Will do. Draft: "Mitigation: revoked broad keystore:decrypt privileges from default node-role; enforced service-account scoping and network egress constraints to KMS proxy; audit logs and request headers augmented to provide caller attribution."
ben: Minor thing - document the rollback steps explicitly: 1) re-add wildcard decrypt role, 2) revert admission webhook, 3) remove netpol. Keep as a short runbook in infra.
carla: Good call. Ben, drop the runbook PR. Dave, once canary stable, we'll schedule full rollout next Tue 09:00 UTC with 1h maintenance window.
ops-bot: NOTE: runbook created at infra/runbooks/rbac-keystore-tighten.md by ben at 1729510360.
carla: Perfect. Thanks everyone - going to queue the admission webhook PR and the keystore-shim header change. If anything unexpected, post here and we'll abort the rollout. :thumbsup:
